extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners preparing or filing ex parte appeals to the PTAB (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for taking an ex parte appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including timing, required papers, content rules, hearing practice, and possible Board outcomes. Focused on U.S. PTO rules and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of ex parte appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative to continuing prosecution before the Examiner; consideration of the application as is, not a forum for making substantive amendments or submitting new evidence; generally results in a decision affirming or reversing the Examiner; the PTAB will not issue a patent — it reviews the Examiner's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an ex parte appeal is available
rubrics_metrics.description: During original prosecution: after a twice rejected patent application or a final Office Action by an examiner. After original prosecution (after a patent issues): via reexamination proceeding or reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB panel composition and adjudicative environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Review by a panel of at least three administrative patent judges who have technical backgrounds, are lawyers, and have been appointed by the Secretary of Commerce. A more formal, legal environment within the Office with legal briefing and optional oral argument before panel of judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall appeal process steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine-step procedural sequence: (1) Adverse Decision of the Examiner, (2) Notice of Appeal, (3) Appeal Brief, (4) Examiner’s Answer, (5) Appeal Forwarding Fee + Reply Brief (optional) + Request for Oral Hearing (optional), (6) Oral Hearing (if requested), (7) Board decision, (8) Request for rehearing (optional), (9) Decision on rehearing (if requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the canonical process flow for ex parte appeals to the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of 'adverse decision' (Step 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adverse decision is generally an Office action including a rejection of one or more claims; appeal is taken from the Office action, so the Office action defines the Examiner’s position on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot appeal from every Office action — the application must be twice rejected; the Office action does not have to be final. Source: 35 U.S.C. § 134; 37 C.F.R. §§ 41.31; MPEP § 1204.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal timing and fee (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must give notice that you intend to appeal from the Examiner’s decision and pay an appeal fee. The notice and payment are due 3 months after the mailing date of the Examiner’s decision (e.g., final Office action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period is extendable for 3 additional months (so can be filed as late as 6 months after the decision). Office provides a form: https://www.uspto.gov/sites/default/files/documents/aia0031.pdf. Source: 35 U.S.C. § 41(a)(6)(A); 37 C.F.R. § 41.31(a); MPEP § 1204.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must include form, fee payment, extension of time (if applicable), signature information, and patent application information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the USPTO form fields and signature/fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Brief timing (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee is due with the Appeal Brief. The Appeal Brief is due 2 months after filing the Notice of Appeal; this time period is extendable for 5 additional months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.37; MPEP § 1205.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and function of the Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeal Brief is a legal brief (not a form) that includes your arguments and defines the appeal. It identifies the issues the judges will consider on appeal; the judges generally will not go looking for issues and if an argument is not raised in the Appeal Brief it may be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must clearly frame issues for the Board; do not assume the judges will find favorable issues not raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new evidence or substantive amendment in appeal papers
rubrics_metrics.description: No new evidence or substantive amendment may be submitted with the Appeal Brief (and generally throughout appeal filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal is a review of the existing record; exceptions are narrow and governed by rules. Source: 37 C.F.R. §§ 41.33, 41.37(c); MPEP §§ 1205, 1206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required sections of the Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeal Brief must include certain sections: Real party in interest; Related matters (e.g., appeals, AIA proceedings, district court cases); Summary of the claimed subject matter; Argument; Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pro se appellant needs to only 'substantially comply' with certain requirements shown in bold. Source: 37 C.F.R. §§ 41.33, 41.37(c); MPEP §§ 1205, 1206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and form requirements (37 C.F.R. § 41.37(c)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments with respect to each ground of rejection must state the basis therefor, with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on; explain why the examiner erred for each ground contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52, any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board. Each ground contested must be argued under a separate heading, and each heading shall reasonably identify the ground (e.g., by claim number, statutory basis, and applied reference, if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer (Step 4) content and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner’s Answer is the Examiner’s response to the Appeal Brief: the Examiner will respond to all of the arguments in the Appeal Brief and will consider whether to maintain or modify each rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Answer includes sections such as Grounds of Rejection to Be Reviewed on Appeal, Withdrawn Rejection(s), New Ground(s) of Rejection, and Response to Arguments. Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.39; MPEP § 1207.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee timing and payment (Step 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal forwarding fee is due 2 months after the Examiner’s Answer and is NOT EXTENDABLE. It may be filed with the Reply Brief (optional) and/or request for oral hearing (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office provides a form for payment: https://www.uspto.gov/sites/default/files/forms/aia0034.pdf. No fee for the Reply Brief; request for oral hearing requires a fee. Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.45; MPEP §§ 1208, 1208.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Brief rules (Step 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply Brief is optional, due 2 months after Examiner’s Answer (NOT EXTENDABLE). Only one reply brief is permitted; there is no fee for filing a reply brief, and it should be submitted at the same time as payment of the appeal forwarding fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Brief content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply Brief is a legal brief (not a form); no new evidence or amendment; no new arguments that were not raised in the Appeal Brief unless they are responsive to an argument in the Examiner’s Answer or addressing a new ground of rejection in the Examiner’s Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limitation on new matters in the reply — it is largely responsive. Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.41(b); MPEP § 1208.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing and fee (Step 5/6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for an oral hearing is optional and due 2 months after the Examiner’s Answer or on the date of filing a Reply Brief, whichever is earlier — NOT EXTENDABLE. Must include payment of a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing procedural expectations (Step 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, the Office will notify you of the hearing date and you must reply to confirm attendance. Attendance may be in person, telephonically, or via video connection. Although rare, the Examiner may appear. Decorum is required at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.47; MPEP § 1209.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing presentation limits and format
rubrics_metrics.description: You will have 20 minutes to present your case to three judges (who may attend remotely). Judges will have already read the record on appeal and may or may not ask questions. No new arguments or evidence are permitted absent a showing of good cause based on a recent, relevant decision of the PTAB or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise oral presentation because judges are familiar with the record; new matters are generally barred. Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.47; MPEP § 1209.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision outcomes and definitions (Step 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will issue a written decision after considering all arguments and the record. Outcomes include: Affirmance (each claim subject to a sustained rejection — no non-rejected claim), Affirmance-in-Part (at least one claim, but not all, subject to a sustained rejection), Reversed (no claim subject to a rejection — no sustained rejections), or New Ground(s) of Rejection (judges issue a new rejection of one or more claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: 37 C.F.R. § 41.50; MPEP § 1213.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Board outcomes and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome dictates who is responsible for taking the next step: if affirmance or new ground(s) of rejection, the appellant must take the next step; if affirmance-in-part, appellant may take the next step; if reversal, the Examiner will take the next step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1214 for practical consequences and options after the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method for appeal papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file papers using EFS Web; electronic filing guide is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links: https://www.uspto.gov/patents-application-process/file-online and EFS Web Quick Start Guide. Follow EFS Web filing requirements and formats.
